The prior development TESTS edge records a failed candidate selection; its PRODUCES edges link the aggregate to dependent slices and a provisional mechanism comparison. Neither establishes that local transitions are useless. Source inspection of the current incumbent shows causal convolutions, a 0.1 preceding-state injection in the last block, and a final 0.85 current-state/0.15 preceding-context blend. These observations motivate a distinct item-identity test without establishing a deficit.

attrs.claim: The negative aggregate and mixed direct-versus-state contrast are compatible with no incremental benefit from explicit item identity, sufficient identity in the incumbent, optimization or capacity effects shared by both arms, unequal source-tensor distributions despite normalization, changed gradients to the shared item embedding, or seed, checkpoint, and category variation. The historical local-difference failure is context, not replication of this mechanism.

The candidate adds a zero-initialized, bias-free, 0.1-scaled tanh projection of the normalized current-item embedding. The matched control applies the same-capacity projection to the normalized current encoder state. Source review and host method-scope admission support this implementation description; fixed-state branch-formula discrimination and causal isolation remain unverified.

Candidate minus control by category was +0.008 Movies_and_TV, -0.012 Industrial_and_Scientific, -0.005 Electronics, and +0.001 CDs_and_Vinyl. Candidate minus incumbent was -0.015, +0.010, -0.012, and 0.000 respectively. These negative, mixed, and null contrasts are dependent slices of one development seed. Neither new arm cleared the host baseline-only promotion rule.

gap.suspected_capability: Conditioning each causal convolution residual update on the state entering its block.
gap.task_context: The current model adds each causal convolution update to its block input. The proposed gate tests whether input-dependent scaling of that update helps next-item ranking. Prior graph comparisons test local change and direct item identity, not this block-level interaction; their failed selection does not refute this hypothesis.

method.cost: One learned hidden-width vector and elementwise operations per block in each new arm. GPU runtime is unmeasured. Reserve 1000000 budget units for four development fits per arm, conditional confirmation fits, missing incumbent confirmation fits, and overhead; host costing must verify sufficiency.
method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis. Let x be the block input and y its existing causal convolution update. Add 0.1 × tanh(g ⊙ tanh(x)) ⊙ y to the incumbent output x + y, with learned channel vector g initialized to zero. The matched control substitutes tanh(y) for tanh(x), retaining the same vector, initialization, scale, and operations. This contrasts conditioning on the incoming state with conditioning on the update itself.
